locator.section: 9.6 Ethers (third arrow off the molecular ion, labelled 'i', to m/z 43)

evidence.curator_note: ROUTE 1 OF THREE to m/z 43, and the one the prose says dominates: 'In contrast to the spectra of amines, the most abundant ions, C3H7+ and C5H11+, are produced by charge-site-initiated reactions.' Charge-site heterolysis of the O6-C7 bond straight from the molecular ion: both bonding electrons go to the oxygen, which neutralises it and leaves it holding the odd electron as the pentyloxy radical (C5H11O., 87.0810), while the charge migrates to the isopropyl group (43.0542). One curator-supplied move -- this is exactly the RHS shape of the MOD rule 'inductive_wiki', except for the charge placement defect recorded in the mechanism note -- and the arrow-check reports the expected soft line on atom 6 (a bonding pair becoming a lone pair while the odd electron already there is untouched). The page reaches m/z 43 by THREE drawn routes: this one, from m/z 73 (IMS9-EQ9.37d) and from m/z 71 (IMS9-EQ9.37f); the prose quantifies the split with labelling data, 'Deuterium-labeling indicates that 40% of the base C3H7+ peak arises from further decomposition of C5H11+' -- quoted, not stored, since no percentage is printed on the scheme. ARC COUNT (convention D): ZERO curved arrows in the whole of equation 9.37 -- nine reaction arrows, each carrying only a reaction-type label (alpha, i, rH, and one 'i, - C2H4'), and not one fishhook or two-electron arc on any structure. Every electron move in every record of this equation is therefore curator-supplied. Any record of eq 9.37 claiming drawn electron-pushing would be fabricated. SUBSTRATE: isopropyl pentyl ether, C5H11-O-CH(CH3)2, drawn skeletally with '+.' on the oxygen. The equation carries NO label on the substrate; the compound and its molecular ion are named on the FACING page (PDF 272, printed p261): 'The important primary cleavages of isopropyl pentyl ether (Djerassi and Fenselau 1965) are due to these two types of cleavage (Equation 9.37)', with Figure 9.14 there showing '130M+.'. C8H18O, M+. computed 130.1352 -- and 'm/z 130' is therefore NOT printed in this equation; it is stored as the precursor_mz on the authority of the facing page and is not claimed as a printed label. ATOM MAPS: 1-5 = the pentyl carbons (1 = the CH2 bonded to oxygen, 5 = the terminal methyl), 6 = the oxygen, 7 = the isopropyl methine, 8 and 9 = its two methyls; 10, 11, 12 = the migrating hydrogens where a record needs one explicit. 'THESE TWO TYPES OF CLEAVAGE' names the two channel families the equation draws: alpha-cleavage (the book's radical-site reaction, giving m/z 115 and 73) and charge-site cleavage i (giving m/z 43 and 71). The prose adds the abundance ordering: 'the most abundant ions, C3H7+ and C5H11+, are produced by charge-site-initiated reactions', and 'For the competing alpha-cleavages, the loss of methyl from the tertiary carbon yielding m/z 115 is almost as favorable as the loss of the larger butyl group from the secondary carbon.' MEASUREMENTS (convention F): the page labels SIX m/z values -- 115, 45, 73, 31, 43, 71 -- and every one matches the exact mass computed from the structure encoded here (115.1117, 45.0335, 73.0648, 31.0178, 43.0542, 71.0855; RDKit ExactMolWt, formal charge applied). Only THREE neutral losses are printed ('C5H10' and 'C3H6' as product formulas, and '- C2H4' under one arrow); the others (CH3., C4H9., C5H11O., C3H7O., CH3CHO, CH2O) are curator inferences that close the mass balance exactly and are NOT quoted as printed text. No percentage is printed in the equation; Figure 9.14 on the facing page carries the abundances (43 as base peak, 71 strong, 115 and 130 weak) but it is a figure on another page, so nothing is stored as relative_intensity. *** m/z 43 IS THE ISOPROPYL CATION C3H7+ (43.0542), NOT THE ACETYL CATION C2H3O+ (43.0178). *** The drawn structure contains no oxygen at all -- one central vertex, two methyls, a '+' -- and the prose names C3H7+ explicitly. The same nominal mass means the opposite thing two pages earlier in eq 9.35, where m/z 43 IS the acetyl cation; that contrast is why this is spelled out.

data/mechanisms/rule_index.json has NO chapter-9 entries. *** MEASURED (RDKit substructure counts on this record's instantiated molecular ion), with one genuine rule DEFECT recorded. *** 'inductive_wiki' (wikipedia.py:15, '[C]1[C]2[O+.]3[C]4[C]5 >> [C]1[C]2[O.]3.[C]4[C+]5') embeds TWICE on this ether -- it is the only rule in the set that matches an ionised dialkyl ether, and its LHS is exactly this equation's charge-site geometry, so the i channels ARE reachable in principle. BUT ITS RIGHT-HAND SIDE PUTS THE CHARGE ON THE WRONG CARBON: '[C]4[C+]5' places the '+' on the atom one bond FURTHER from the oxygen than the bond it cleaves, so applying it to this substrate would give a primary cation on an isopropyl methyl, whereas the page draws (and the prose names) the ISOPROPYL cation, charge on the carbon that lost the oxygen. MISMATCH: the rule's geometry is one atom off for a simple charge-site cleavage. That is read from the DFS string, not from running MOD, and it is the same class of defect as the IMS_4_9/4_10/4_11/4_12 geometry bugs already recorded in RESUME.md. TESTED AND REJECTED for the alpha channels: 'alpha' (wikipedia.py:6) gives 0 embeddings (it requires an ionised CARBONYL, and an ether has none) and 'esterMcLafferty_rH' gives 0 for the same reason -- so the two alpha-cleavages that give m/z 115 and 73, and the alkene-eliminating rH steps, have no counterpart tested here: UNTESTED for any other rule, not 'no rule matches'.
